The new description asks for the tiny grain size of attempts 3 and 4 and also requires the bowl.

tonka-beans.reason: I looked at all four pictures and none of them is right. Attempt 1 shows a pile of small, round, crumpled black pieces that look like raisins or currants. They are not elongated, and they lack the long ridges a tonka bean has. Attempts 2, 3 and 4 all show long, thin, curved pods, several times longer than they are wide. Those are vanilla pods or carob-like pods, not tonka beans. A real tonka bean is a single almond-sized seed, about 3 cm long, black, tapered at both ends and deeply wrinkled along its length. The new description sets that size and shape against a familiar almond and spreads the beans out loosely. That should stop the result from turning into either raisins or vanilla pods.

walnut-bread.reason: None of the four pictures works. Attempts 1 and 2 are whole loaves, but no walnuts show anywhere, so nothing marks them as walnut bread. Attempts 3 and 4 show walnut pieces only on a cut face, and a whole loaf is required. The new description asks for an uncut loaf with walnut halves visible on the crust.

watermelon-seeds.reason: I looked at all four images. Attempt 1 is in a bowl, but the pieces are plump and round like broad beans, not flat, tapered watermelon seeds. Attempts 2, 3 and 4 do show the right flat, tapered seeds, but each is a loose heap on a plain surface with no bowl, so they miss the required presentation. None is usable. The new description asks for both things at once: the bowl, and the flat teardrop seed shape with its dark roasted shell.

yuzu-kosho.reason: I opened all four pictures and none can be used. Attempt 1 is in a bowl, but the paste is smooth, glossy and runny, like a pourable sauce, not thick and textured yuzu kosho. Attempts 2, 3 and 4 show the right coarse green paste, but each one is in an open glass jar. A jar counts as packaging, and the brief asks for a bowl. The new description asks for the coarse, grainy paste piled in a mound in an open dish, and it rules out jars and packaging.
